questions: What is the most dangerous assumption?

answers.question: What changed?
answers.answer: Hesai launched Kosmo One and Kosmo World on October 14 as an integrated spatial-capture and 3D reconstruction offering.

answers.question: Whose behavior changed?
answers.answer: actor:hesai:provider-builder performed an inspectable release, funding announcement or research publication; downstream buyer behavior unknown.

answers.question: What problem is demonstrated?
answers.answer: Real-world 3D data capture can be costly and hard to reproduce.

answers.question: Who benefits?
answers.answer: Robotics builders, VFX teams and spatial-content operators could benefit; actual buyers remain unverified.

answers.question: What substitute exists?
answers.answer: Photogrammetry, LiDAR scanners, hand-authored scenes and existing 3DGS pipelines.

answers.question: What mechanism matters?
answers.answer: Time-aligned LiDAR, RGB and IMU data reconstructed as reusable 3DGS assets.

answers.question: What is the most dangerous assumption?
answers.answer: Vendor-reported accuracy and cost improvements will transfer to local client workflows.

answers.question: What would falsify the interpretation?
answers.answer: Independent benchmark finds comparable capture cost, editability or geometry error worse than substitutes.

answers.question: What evidence is missing?
answers.answer: Independent benchmark on challenging materials and lighting; Real licensing and asset-export terms; Paid pilot demand

answers.question: What simpler explanation competes?
answers.answer: Primarily a hardware/cloud platform launch aimed at robotics rather than a new freelance market.
